notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Job 39 this time. My tools stopped working before I managed to read a single page, and your rules say to report only what the sources actually say, so the notes would be empty.

**What happened:** I tried to load six pages at once, all on your approved sites:
- Enduring Word: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-39/
- Ellicott on BibleHub: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/job/39.htm
- Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/job/39.htm
- Gill on BibleHub: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/job/39.htm
- NET Bible notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Job+39
- Wesley's Notes on StudyLight: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wes/job-39.html

The code I wrote to unpack the results had a bug, and it crashed before showing me any text. When I tried to fix it, the tool told me I had used up my allowance of calls for this turn. So I don't know what any of those pages say, or even whether they all loaded.

I could fill in verse notes from what I generally know about Job 39, but that would break your rule against filling gaps from my own knowledge. It also wouldn't match the URLs I'd be giving you, so I haven't done it.

**What I'll do when you ask again:**
1. **The usual reading:** read the six pages above verse by verse, adding Precept Austin and Matthew Henry, Barnes or Clarke on BibleHub or StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** search Ligonier, Desiring God, Grace to You, Spurgeon, Seedbed, the Wesley Center and the Lutheran sites for Job 39 or Job 38–41. It's worth knowing in advance that this chapter may not split along denominational lines. If I find no real differences, I'll say so rather than make some up.
3. **Other views:**
   - Bible Odyssey on the speeches God gives from the whirlwind.
   - The NET Bible's notes on the hard-to-translate words, especially the ostrich and stork in v. 13 and the "wild ox" in v. 9.
   - Church Fathers on New Advent, such as Gregory the Great's *Morals on Job*, which covers this chapter.
   - Any material on Catholic.com or the Orthodox Church in America's site.

I'll include popular modern teaching such as prosperity or word of faith only if those sites actually discuss it in connection with this chapter.

Just reply "go ahead" and I'll do the research and write the notes in your "v. 1: …" format, with a URL after every point.
